full_judgment:
2. The petitioner's case is that he worked for 20 years in the Crescent Jute Mills Company Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "the Company) from the inception of the Mill and after the nationalisation of the Jute Mills by the Govt. he was promoted as the Manager and Project-in-charge of the Company on 14.10.72 While the petitioner was expecting a further promotion certain people who were junior to him and some interested persons started conspiring against the petitioner and at the instance of such people Bangladesh Jute Industries Corporation (hereinafter referred to as the Corporation) by its office order dated 15.10.73 transferred the petitioner from the company to the head office of the Corporation under Director (T) Section with immediate effect the petitioner handed over the charge of the Company and Mill to one Mr. Nazirul Islam on 31.10.73. The order of transfer did not disclose the rank, status or the designation of the petitioner. The Corporation, however, by its order dated 6.12.73 informed the petitioner that he is transferred to the Head Office as Manager under Director (T) Section to look after the work of Chittagong Zone in the pay and pay-scale he was drawing at Crescent Jute Mills Company Limited. The Company had for a long time scheme of gratuity and a Provident Fund Scheme. The Corporation never took charge of these schemes nor does it have any prescribed scheme for all the nationalised companies. When the petitioner handed over the charge he also settled his account with the Company. He took Tk. 50,000/-as his gratuity for 20 months up to 8.2.73 and also received money he was entitled to under the Companies Provident Fund Scheme including Tk. 15,339.79 being 100% companies contribution to his Provident Fund. After a period of 4 months of his joining the head office of the Corporation the petitioner was surprised to receive the impugned order dated 8.2.74 alleging that the petitioner's withdrawal of gratuity and Provident Fund contribution was highly irregular and he was further placed under suspension with immediate effect. The petitioner submitted an explanation on 14.2.74 as he was asked for and requested the Corporation to exonerate him from any offence that he might have committed. After waiting for some time the petitioner's learned Advocate sent a demand of justice notice to the respondents on 17.3.74 by a telegram requesting withdrawal of the order of suspension. Two days later this application was moved in this court. 

 6. After perusal of the petitioner and the affidavit-in-opposition and Annexures annexed thereto, we find that the Corporation, long before the petitioner was ordered to be transferred from the Company to the Corporation, decided on 25.11.72 that the service of Chief Executives including the Manager to be transferable from one Jute Mill to another or to the Corporation with continuity of service, and on transfer to the Corporation's Head Office a fresh appointment letter will be given to the individual incumbent and allow him continuity of service and for this personal file service records and Provident Fund account of the person concerned be also transferred to the Project of Corporation head office where the incumbent is posted or transferred. The petitioner has also insisted in his correspondence addressed to the corporation on continuation of terms and emoluments of his service. It is clear that while the petitioner was transferred from the company to the Corporation, his service was not interrupted. As the petitioner's service did not come to an end on his transfer, the Corporation thought that his withdrawal of the gratuity and his entitlement from the Provident Fund was irregular. We refrain from making any comment on the alleged irregularity or illegality in the withdrawal in question as the whole matter is yet to be thrashed out in the proceeding that is to follow the impugned order of suspension.
